title: VaultNote
description: An atomic note of a project's vault (ADR 0049). `created` and `updated` are when the thing became known and when what the note says last changed; `edition` marks a notebook that reports one working session; `task_id` is the task it was written under.

note_id.title: VaultNoteId
note_id.description: A note's identifier, unique within a project: kebab-case words that say what the note is (`macro-tokenizer`, not `note-12`). It is what `[[id]]` links and `![[id]]` embeds name, so it does not change.

project_id.title: ProjectId
project_id.description: Stable project identifier (lowercase slug). Never a path; paths live in the local registry.

type.title: VaultNoteType
type.description: What a note is. concept: a fundamental, independent of any experiment. method: how this project builds or does something. experiment: one study and its protocol. finding: what was observed, with its numbers and limits. claim: what is believed, with a standing. decision: a choice made and why. question: something not known yet. log: process worth keeping that is not knowledge. figure: a chart, table or visualisation drawn from the project's runs by code the note carries (ADR 0053). notebook: a compilation of embedded notes with connecting prose.

title.description: A claim, finding or decision is titled with a sentence that states it; a concept or method with its name; a question with the question.

gist.description: One sentence that says the thing itself (not a description of the note). The first of the three depths.

summary.description: Two to four sentences that continue from the gist without restating it. For a notebook: its opening paragraph, what it establishes and how it proceeds. Markdown with LaTeX, `[[id]]` links.

full.description: The rest, continuing from the summary without restating it. `![[id]]` alone on a line embeds another note at that point. For a notebook: the composition, connecting prose and embeds, optionally under `##` headings.

standing.title: VaultStanding
standing.description: Where a claim, decision or question stands. claim: established, leaning, open or ruled_out. decision: in_force, proposed or superseded. question: open or answered. Other types carry none.

key.title: VaultKey
key.description: The one number or comparison that carries the note, and what it is.

support.description: Claims: how much evidence, plainly (runs, seeds, scale).

would_change.description: Claims: what result would move the standing.

items.title: VaultEvidence
items.description: One run a note rests on.

run.description: A run of the project, by run name (or MLflow run ID). Its values are read from the run when the note is shown: a note never stores a metric value here.

role.description: What the run is to the note.

vs.description: The baseline run this row is compared with, when a note has more than one baseline.

figure.title: VaultFigure
figure.description: Figures: the code that draws the figure (ADR 0053). The gist says in words what it shows; the runs it draws from are its `evidence`.

script.description: JavaScript, run as the body of an async function in a sandboxed frame with no network: `el` is the element to draw into, `ak` reads the project's runs (`ak.runs.list({filter, limit})`, `ak.runs.get(id)`, `ak.runs.history(id, key)`, `ak.artifacts.list(id, path)`, `ak.artifacts.preview(id, path)`) and gives the theme (`ak.theme`), and `Plot` and `d3` are Observable Plot and d3. Read every number from the runs: never write one in.

study.description: Experiments: the study record whose variants this note describes.

aliases.description: Concepts and methods: other words the term goes by (an abbreviation, a plural), so a mention in another note's prose finds this note.

bears_on.description: Questions: the claims an answer would move.

items.title: VaultNoteId
items.description: A note's identifier, unique within a project: kebab-case words that say what the note is (`macro-tokenizer`, not `note-12`). It is what `[[id]]` links and `![[id]]` embeds name, so it does not change.

cites.description: The prior work the note rests on, from the project's library, each with its role. Shown with the note; exported as citations.

items.title: VaultCite
items.description: One work of the library a note cites, with the role it plays there.

work.title: VaultWorkId
work.description: A work's identifier in the project's library, also its citation key: kebab-case, the first author's family name, the year and a word of the title (`vaswani-2017-attention`), or the project and owner for code (`karpathy-nanogpt`). It does not change.

role.title: VaultCiteRole
role.description: The part a work plays in a note. background: explains something the note rests on. method: the note's method is taken or adapted from it. solution: it showed how to get past a problem the note records (a fix, a setting, a workaround). baseline: its method or reported result is what the note compares against. supports: it reports what the note says. contradicts: it reports otherwise. inspiration: it suggested what to try, not how. tool: its code, data or model is used.

where.description: Where in the work: a section, equation, table, figure, page or file.

note.description: What exactly was taken from it, or how the note departs from it.

sources.description: Where the note was distilled from, as `kind:id` (`task:…`, `run:…`, `study:…`, a research record kind) or `repo:<path>` for a file in the project's repository. Provenance, shown last.

task_id.title: TaskId
task_id.description: AblationKit task identifier (UI- or agent-first task).

created_at.title: Timestamp
created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with a `Z` suffix and optional fractional seconds.

updated_at.title: Timestamp
updated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with a `Z` suffix and optional fractional seconds.

created_by.title: ResearchActor
created_by.description: Who made a change: a human session, an agent token or the system. Work under a task links the task (`task:ID`).

updated_by.title: ResearchActor
updated_by.description: Who made a change: a human session, an agent token or the system. Work under a task links the task (`task:ID`).

archived_at.title: Timestamp
archived_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with a `Z` suffix and optional fractional seconds.
